edit.description: `waveMergeError` carries a verdict for every cause, the way `waveSlotThrow` beside it already does
the non-ledger merge throw driven end to end through a wave that already shipped a span

summary: `waveMergeError` wraps every merge throw, not the ledger refusal alone — a wave's settled facts reach no surface otherwise

per.section: A fact the engine holds is reported, never rediscovered

acceptance: A fanout wave whose merge stage throws outside `commitPendingUpdate` leaves as a `WaveCarriedThrow`, so `tick()` returns `failed: true` with `verdict` set and no `ledgerRefusal` rather than re-throwing at `src/Dispatcher.ts:1090`; the ledger-refusal arm keeps the class it reports today.
tests: a wave whose merge stage throws outside its ledger rewrite reports a tick verdict naming the spans it already shipped
a non-ledger throw out of a wave's merge stage reports no ledger-refusal class
notes: `w.refusal` is set only by `commitAttemptLedger`, while `mergeError` (`src/waveTick.ts:456`) holds every throw out of `mergeAttempt` — so `src/waveMerge.ts:1101` returns bare and the tick loses its shipped tags, usage rows and merge-outcome shas. `settledWaveVerdict`'s own doc already states the rule the carry does not follow. One reachable lever: an afterMerge gate that reds over a prior-attempt slot that will not write.
